August 18, 2026

Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield  
Attn: Grievances and Appeals  
P.O. Box 518  
North Haven, CT 06473-0518

Re: Appeal of Prior Authorization Denial  
Member: Emerson Foster  
Member ID: W511360146  
Requested service: Arthroscopic rotator cuff repair  
CPT: 29827  
Reference number: POC-BB2C61BC1B-86183  
Date of denial notice: August 18, 2026

Dear Grievances and Appeals Department:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827. The denial states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity.

The available Anthem/Carelon Joint Surgery guideline identifies the following criteria:

“Pain ≥ 3 on the VAS scale which interferes with age-appropriate activities of daily living.”

“Physical exam consistent with symptomatic rotator cuff tear (e.g., drop arm test, painful arc, full/empty can test, weakness of internal/external rotation or abduction).”

“Recent advanced imaging confirms features of a degenerative full thickness tear.”

“Failure of at least 6 weeks of conservative management.”

The records address each of these requirements:

- I have had 14 months of progressive shoulder pain that has not improved with rest.
- The pain substantially interferes with daily activities. I cannot lift my arm above shoulder height and cannot sleep on the affected side.
- The June 15, 2026 MRI documents a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm, with grade 2 fatty atrophy.
- Examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.
- I completed 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics, including 24 visits from April 6, 2026, through July 27, 2026.
- I used NSAIDs for six months without adequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on June 2, 2026, provided only four weeks of partial relief.
- The clinical record does not identify an active infection or untreated substance-use issue. My BMI is 29, and I am a nonsmoker.

The documentation therefore establishes a symptomatic, MRI-confirmed full-thickness rotator cuff tear, persistent functional impairment, and failure of substantially more than six weeks of conservative treatment. The records also show that nonoperative treatment, including supervised therapy, medication, and injection, has not provided durable relief.

Please overturn the denial and authorize CPT 29827. If Anthem maintains the denial, please provide the complete clinical-review rationale, identify every item of documentation considered missing, and provide the exact medical-necessity criteria and guideline version applied to this request. The denial notice did not identify the specific criteria or missing records.

Please acknowledge receipt of this appeal and provide the appeal determination in writing.

Sincerely,

Emerson Foster  
Member ID: W511360146
